objective: Test one explicitly predeclared past-only volatility gate on lookback-5 momentum through the existing regime-stability and null framework.
observed_effect: The volatility-gated momentum strategy showed CONSISTENT_WITH_NOISE verdicts across all 10 assets (AMZN, JPM, and 8 others), while the base momentum showed REGIME_STABLE (AMZN) and REGIME_DEPENDENT (JPM) evidence. The V_THRESHOLD=0.20 gate eliminated all momentum signals because realized volatility consistently exceeded the threshold, falsifying the hypothesis that a single past-only volatility gate improves momentum robustness.
primary_question: Does a single past-only volatility gate create a predeclared robustness improvement for the qualified momentum effect?
uncertainty_reduced: The volatility gate mechanism (V_THRESHOLD=0.20 on trailing realized volatility) is now falsified as a robustness enhancer for lookback-5 momentum. The persistence of base momentum suggests the gate may be too restrictive or that the volatility threshold chosen does not capture meaningful regime separation for this signal class.
